title: Flood buyouts can reduce physical exposure while distributing compensation and relocation gains unequally
source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35726; federal property acquisitions, housing sales, restricted-use Census microdata, and individual movement records
geography: United States; nationwide federal flood-property buyouts and post-buyout neighborhood movement

observations.period: federal flood buyouts and longer-run moves studied through 2026; paper issued September 2026

compensation_gap.value: households of color received at least 6% lower buyout compensation than White households
compensation_gap.unit: compensation relative to property fair-market value

white_relocation.value: White participants relocated to higher-quality neighborhoods and were better off than White nonparticipants

black_relocation.value: Black participants moved to worse neighborhoods and were worse off than Black nonparticipants

policy_interface.value: the study treats buyouts as a climate-adaptation policy whose compensation and relocation route can shape longer-run neighborhood outcomes

observations.method: The authors combine nationwide administrative data on federal property acquisitions, housing sales transactions, restricted-use Census microdata, and a database tracking individual movement over time. They compare buyout compensation with fair-market value and examine neighborhood outcomes by race and participation.
observations.uncertainty: This is a working paper and the public abstract does not provide every specification, sample restriction, or mechanism. The reported comparisons do not by themselves establish why compensation differs, whether every participant had a comparable alternative, or whether all later wellbeing outcomes moved with neighborhood quality.
observations.subgroup: White, Black, and other households of color participating or not participating in federal flood-property buyouts; race, property characteristics, local housing markets, program administration, and destination neighborhoods vary.
observations.counterinterpretation: Differences may reflect property appraisal, bargaining, timing, selection into buyouts, prior wealth, local market conditions, eligibility, or unmeasured household constraints. A move to a higher- or lower-quality neighborhood is not the same as improved or worsened health, security, belonging, or political trust.

related_sources.claim: NBER DOI record for Working Paper 35726

boundary: This record adds a climate-adaptation and unequal-mobility finding: leaving physical flood exposure can still involve unequal compensation and destination outcomes. It does not establish a universal racial mechanism, a causal effect of every buyout program, or complete household wellbeing after relocation.
